solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dance with sailor the wrong way after drink

indicators.note: after tells us the turned sailor follows the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a common drink

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the sailor's letters run backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A dancer partners a sailor who stumbles about after one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: AB (able seaman) is the stock sailor; 'the wrong way' signals the reversal and 'after' the order.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Male teacher upset over what in Spain is saucy

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
que is Spanish for what

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is shocked by something racy he hears in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals reading the teacher's title upwards; 'over' sets it above the Spanish word in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué means slightly indecent, close in sense to saucy as in a saucy seaside postcard.

clue.text: Theatrical actor with dilemma to be resolved

indicators.note: a dilemma to be resolved suggests its letters, with the actor's, need sorting into a new order

explanation.surface: A dramatic performer faces a tricky choice that must be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be resolved' rearranges ACTOR plus DILEMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodramatic means exaggerated and showy, a synonym for theatrical in its figurative sense.

clue.text: React if I made a mess of trick

indicators.note: making a mess of something jumbles it, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they botched a trick by how they reacted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a mess of' rearranges REACT, IF and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is clever deception, a synonym of trick or ruse.

clue.text: Request a very quiet meal with no starter

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

indicators.note: a meal with no starter loses its first course, so the word drops its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a hushed dinner, skipping the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no starter' takes M off MEAL to leave EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal is an earnest request, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Trouble over Republican — one committing perjury

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word for trouble runs backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: A political row over a Republican who lied under oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a placement word but here signals turning the trouble word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is lying under oath, so someone committing it tells falsehoods.

clue.text: Fashionable legal document? I'll say!

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a deed is a signed legal document, such as one transferring property

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses about a trendy legal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic interjections of agreement, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Chap making good agent and pilot

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
an airman flies aircraft, as a pilot does

explanation.surface: A man succeeds as both a sales agent and an aviator.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to mend, so a man who fixes broken things fits.

clue.text: Nasty affair making one be serious

parts.note: mean means nasty or unkind
business means an affair or matter, as in a bad business

explanation.surface: An unpleasant scandal forces someone to get serious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be in earnest about one's intentions.

clue.text: Hints about crossing large Croatian resort

indicators.note: crossing means the reversed hints go across the letter for large, holding it inside
about means turned about, so the word for hints is read backwards

parts.note: tips are hints or useful advice
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Travel tips about crossing to a big Croatian holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TIPS to SPIT, and 'crossing' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a port city on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia and a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Individual initially anti-beer stupidly gets drunk

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word for one person
acting stupidly suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teetotal campaigner foolishly ends up intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' signals the anagram of the hyphenated word; 'drunk' is a noun here, a person who drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, so it matches drunk used as a noun.

clue.text: One used to listen to nobleman mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the nobleman's title loses its last letter

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone is told to heed what a lord says, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing is the body part used for listening.

clue.text: I criticise severely a poor Asian capital

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly
bad means poor in quality

explanation.surface: A critic confesses to panning a weak performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan, in South Asia.

clue.text: Fighters in rings somehow used to dramas

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive in some unexplained order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Boxers who are somehow accustomed to theatrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges TO DRAMAS; the rings are bullrings, not boxing rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Matadors kill bulls in the circular arena of a bullring, so they fight in rings.

clue.text: Able to be a contestant, not losing heart

parts.note: to compete is to take part as a contestant

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word not is removed

explanation.surface: Fit to enter a contest without becoming discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent means having the necessary skill, a synonym for able.

clue.text: Plant found in the shade around lake

indicators.note: around means the shelter word goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: cover can mean shade or shelter from the sun
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A plant growing in the shadows near a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing plant with three-part leaves, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Former partner takes steps producing demands

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
to take steps is to act, so acts

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse goes to court with demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain, so exacts is a verb synonym of demands.

clue.text: Energy old man's needed after retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the father's word runs backwards

parts.note: pa is a word for father, the old man, so pa's

explanation.surface: Dad needs a boost of energy now he has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Sap means vigour or vitality, as in full of sap, a sense of energy.

clue.text: Where food may be — in crack at bottom of cooking vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, at bottom of places the attempt below the vessel

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
a crack is an attempt, as in have a crack at, so a try

explanation.surface: Food found trapped in a crack on the underside of a saucepan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at bottom of' puts TRY under PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a larder, a small room or cupboard where food is stored.

clue.text: From where child may feed tame animal immediately

definitions.text: From where child may feed tame animal
definitions.meaning: a child feeding a pet holds food on the palm, so the food comes from that spot

explanation.surface: A child feeding a pet straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at once, without thinking, as when rejecting an idea summarily.

clue.text: Sound made by turkey perhaps is very unpleasant

indicators.note: sound made by signals the word is heard, not seen, so a bird word gives a like-sounding one

parts.note: a turkey is an example of a fowl, a farmyard bird

explanation.surface: The gobble of a turkey is a nasty noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound made by' tells us FOWL is said, giving its homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul means disgusting or offensive, a synonym of very unpleasant.

clue.text: Concealed, not originally being observable

indicators.note: not originally means without its first letter, so the word for concealed is beheaded

parts.note: covert means secret or concealed

explanation.surface: Something hidden that was not at first visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not originally' drops C from COVERT, which turns it into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and plainly visible, a synonym of observable.

clue.text: Meet first couple of entertainers by bar

indicators.note: a couple is two, so the opening two letters of the performers' word are taken

parts.note: a counter is a bar where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Arrange to meet two of the first performers beside the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first couple of' takes EN from ENTERTAINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to meet them, often unexpectedly.

clue.text: Cowardly member of family, extremely scrawny

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a family member

indicators.note: extremely takes the two extremes, the outer letters, of the thin word

explanation.surface: A very thin relative who is also timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SY, the outside letters of SCRAWNY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sissy is an informal adjective for timid or weak, close to cowardly.
